## Geographic distribution
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Yakut_language&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geographic distribution")]
Yakut is spoken mainly in the [Sakha Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakha_Republic "Sakha Republic"). It is also used by ethnic Yakuts in [Khabarovsk Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khabarovsk_Region "Khabarovsk Region") and a small diaspora in other parts of the [Russian Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Federation "Russian Federation"), [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan"), [Turkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey "Turkey") and other parts of the world. [Dolgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolgan_language "Dolgan language"), a close relative of Yakut, which formerly was considered by some a dialect of Yakut,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakut_language#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAntonov1997-7) is spoken by [Dolgans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolgans "Dolgans") in [Krasnoyarsk Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krasnoyarsk_Region "Krasnoyarsk Region"). Yakut is widely used as a [lingua franca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lingua_franca "Lingua franca") by other ethnic minorities in the [Sakha Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakha_Republic "Sakha Republic") – more [Dolgans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolgans "Dolgans"), [Evenks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evenks "Evenks"), [Evens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evens "Evens") and [Yukagirs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yukagirs "Yukagirs") speak Yakut rather than their own languages. About 8% of people of ethnicities other than Yakut living in Sakha claimed knowledge of the Yakut language in the [2002 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Russian_Census "2002 Russian Census").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakut_language#cite_note-8)
